topic: Structuring prompts with XML tags: separating instructions, context and input so the model doesn't misread them
text:
Your prompt mixes instructions, pasted data and a question in one blob. The model has to guess where one ends and the next begins.

Anthropic's prompting docs say wrapping each type of content in its own tag (<instructions>, <context>, <input>) reduces misinterpretation, especially when a prompt mixes instructions, context, examples and variable inputs.

Two rules from the same page:
• Use consistent, descriptive tag names across your prompts.
• Nest tags when content has a natural hierarchy, like <documents> containing <document index="1">.

My rule of thumb: the moment a prompt has a variable part (a user message, a scraped page, an email), I'd put it in its own tag and keep the instructions outside it. It also makes the prompt easier to diff and review in a pull request.

Do you template your prompts in code with tags like this, or keep them as free-form text?
